findings.title: Options object flips the documented clearQueue rejection default
findings.cause: The options destructuring uses `rejectOnClear = true` when callers pass an object, while the public docs and types state the default is false. `clearQueue()` then rejects every pending item whenever that unintended truthy default is active.
findings.impact: Code that upgrades to the options form, for example `pLimit({concurrency: 1})`, gets AbortError rejections from pending tasks on `clearQueue()` even though the documented default should only discard the queue. This can turn teardown paths into unexpected rejections or failed Promise.all calls.
findings.evidence: `index.js:4-8` initializes `rejectOnClear` to false but changes the object default to true; `index.js:77-88` rejects queued promises when it is truthy. `index.d.ts:99-106` and `readme.md:46-52` document `Default: false`.
findings.reproduction_or_test: `node --input-type=module -e "import pLimit from './index.js'; const limit=pLimit({concurrency:1}); const p1=limit(()=>new Promise(()=>{})); const p2=limit(()=>Promise.resolve('never')); await Promise.resolve(); limit.clearQueue(); const outcome=await Promise.race([p2.then(()=> 'resolved', error => error?.name || 'rejected'), Promise.resolve().then(()=>Promise.resolve()).then(()=> 'pending')]); if (outcome !== 'pending') throw new Error('default clearQueue should leave pending promise pending, got '+outcome); void p1;"` fails with `got AbortError`.

findings.title: Falsy non-boolean rejectOnClear values bypass validation
findings.cause: The type guard is conditional on the value being truthy: `if (rejectOnClear && typeof rejectOnClear !== 'boolean')`. Falsy non-booleans such as `0`, `''`, or `null` are accepted.
findings.impact: The API claims `rejectOnClear` is boolean-only, but callers can pass invalid values and get silent false-like behavior. That makes input validation inconsistent and can hide configuration bugs.
findings.evidence: `index.js:12-14` only throws for truthy non-booleans. `index.d.ts:99-106` and `readme.md:46-52` define the option as boolean.
findings.reproduction_or_test: `node --input-type=module -e "import pLimit from './index.js'; try { pLimit({concurrency:1, rejectOnClear:0}); } catch { process.exit(0); } throw new Error('non-boolean rejectOnClear=0 was accepted');"` fails because the invalid value is accepted.

findings.title: limit.map drops mapper indexes for non-array iterables
findings.cause: The implementation passes `iterableIsArray ? index : undefined` to the mapper, even though `Array.from` supplies a stable index for every iterable it consumes.
findings.impact: Mappers over Sets, generators, and iterator objects receive `undefined` instead of the documented numeric index. This breaks callers that depend on ordering or pair each item with its position.
findings.evidence: `index.js:106-115` computes `iterableIsArray` and suppresses indexes for non-arrays. `index.d.ts:29-43` and `readme.md:78-84` state that the mapper receives the item value and its index and that the method is equivalent to `Array.from(iterable, (item, index) => limit(mapperFunction, item, index))`.
findings.reproduction_or_test: `node --input-type=module -e "import pLimit from './index.js'; const seen=[]; await pLimit(1).map(new Set(['a','b']), (value,index)=>seen.push([value,index])); const expected=JSON.stringify([['a',0],['b',1]]); const actual=JSON.stringify(seen); if(actual!==expected) throw new Error('bad map indexes: '+actual);"` fails with `bad map indexes: [["a",null],["b",null]]` (`undefined` stringifies as null in arrays).

findings.title: limitFunction ignores arguments passed to the returned wrapper
findings.cause: The wrapper returned by `limitFunction` is `() => limit(() => function_())`, so it discards every argument supplied by the caller.
findings.impact: The named helper only works for zero-argument functions. Any typed or documented use where the limited function accepts parameters receives `undefined` values and can return wrong results or fail at runtime.
findings.evidence: `index.js:121-125` returns a zero-argument wrapper. `index.d.ts:133-136` declares the return type as `(...arguments_: Arguments) => Promise<ReturnType>` and the main limiter contract at `index.d.ts:45-56` says arguments are passed through to `fn`.
findings.reproduction_or_test: `node --input-type=module -e "import {limitFunction} from './index.js'; const lf=limitFunction((a,b)=>a+b,{concurrency:1}); const value=await lf(2,3); if(value!==5) throw new Error('limitFunction did not pass arguments; got '+value);"` fails with `got NaN`.

findings.title: Positive Infinity concurrency is rejected after an edge-case regression
findings.cause: The validator now requires `Number.isInteger(concurrency) && concurrency > 0`, removing the previous allowance for `concurrency === Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY`.
findings.impact: Callers using `pLimit(Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY)` as an unlimited/no-op limiter now get a TypeError. That is a behavior regression for an edge case that the prior validator explicitly supported.
findings.evidence: `index.js:127-130` rejects all non-integers, including `Infinity`. `git diff -- index.js` shows the previous validator accepted `(Number.isInteger(concurrency) || concurrency === Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY) && concurrency > 0`.
findings.reproduction_or_test: `node --input-type=module -e "import pLimit from './index.js'; pLimit(Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY);"` throws `TypeError: Expected \`concurrency\` to be a number from 1 and up`.
